Brazilian court orders Apple to tighten age controls on a casino-style app on the App Store, including requiring age verification before in-app purchases. Details below.

Brazil orders Apple to strengthen App Store age screening

According to Tilt, a court in São Paulo has approved a preliminary injunction requiring Apple to restrict minors from accessing the "Casino Roulette: Roulettist" app.

In July this year, four children's and adolescents' rights organisations filed a civil lawsuit alleging that minors were able to download casino-style games from the App Store and purchase virtual chips with real money, despite Casino Roulette: Roulettist having an age restriction of 18 and above, leading the court to issue the ruling.

Tilt reported that the court gave Apple five days in its ruling to prohibit users registered as minors from newly downloading Casino Roulette: Roulettist, and required "the establishment of an age verification procedure for purchasing virtual chips with real money to continue playing or expand the in-app experience".

Beyond that specific app, the ruling also prohibits Apple from listing new apps with equivalent casino-style mechanics on the App Store unless effective age control measures are in place.

Tilt reported that the court also required Apple to preserve all records related to the app and submit a technical report detailing the measures taken. The court also set a daily fine of 100,000 reais (approximately US$19,500) for violations.

Tilt has contacted Apple regarding the matter and requested a response, but had not received a reply by deadline.
